* fix(storage): bound a MERGE's node-key wait by the resolved transaction timeout, release the ended transaction at once and log prolonged waits, 0 disabling either (v1.4.4) (#1756)
A MERGE that waits for a uniquely constrained node key another transaction
holds (#1673) had no server-side bound: with no client deadline it waited
until the holder ended, indefinitely for an abandoned transaction, and
nothing logged the wait. The configured transaction timeout
(database.transaction_timeout, NORNICDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT) was read but
used nowhere.
The config package now resolves its disableable duration settings, the
transaction timeout and the slow-query threshold, through one owner
(pkg/config/disableable_duration.go) with explicit semantics for every
source: an empty value is unset, 0 disables the setting, a positive
duration or whole seconds sets it, and a negative or invalid value stops
startup naming its source. Precedence: the default, the YAML key, then the
environment variables, the first set one winning (a set
NORNICDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT, 0 included, suppresses the legacy
NEO4J_dbms_transaction_timeout). Before, an environment zero for either
setting was ignored and left the file or default value. Every slow-query
reporter (the Cypher slow-query log and metric, the HTTP slow-query log)
decides through one helper, SlowQueryThresholdReached, so a zero threshold
reports nothing; the HTTP log used to report every query at zero.
The engine takes a lock-wait policy (EngineOptions.LockWait) that
pkg/nornicdb fills from the resolved timeout and slow-query threshold,
through one startup owner (resolveEngineOptions) for persistent and
in-memory databases. MERGE key admission, the one owner every MERGE route
uses, passes it to the key-lock registry's wait; commit-time waits pass
none and are unchanged. Timers are armed only when the MERGE actually
blocks and are pooled, and the timeout counts from the start of the wait
across wake-ups. A MERGE that waits the timeout fails with
Neo.ClientError.Transaction.TransactionTimedOut; a wait past the slow-query
threshold logs one localized storage.transaction.lock_wait_prolonged
warning naming both transactions. Client deadlines, cancellation and
deadlock detection end the wait as before.
A failure that ends an explicit transaction (memory limit, server or client
transaction timeout, TERMINATE TRANSACTIONS) rolls its native storage back
at once at the one cleanup owner (failTransaction), as memory failures
already did: its keys and write admission are released even if the client
stays idle, and the transaction stays failed until its owner ends it.
Tests over Bolt (driver and raw), HTTP and the Cypher API (auto-commit and
explicit, both parsers), persistent and in-memory databases, every source
combination of both settings, the storage owner and every Cypher MERGE
route; a benchmark of uncontended and contended MERGE writers under the
default configuration.

* fix: sync the configuration fcv counters with the shipped template (#1021)
conf/collector.conf declares conf.version and common/fcv.go declares
FcvConfiguration.CurrentVersion, but nothing tied the two together. 810acbf
raised CurrentVersion 10->12 while 0fbb387 moved the template 13->14, so the
counters drifted apart and LowestConfigurationVersion stopped at key 12.
There is no runtime symptom today. CurrentVersion is never read -- only
FcvCheckpoint.CurrentVersion is, by ckpt_manager.go -- and the single CheckFcv
call site passes FeatureCompatibleVersion=10, which the template's 14 always
satisfies. The exposure is the upgrade hint: check.go renders
LowestConfigurationVersion[fcv], and a missing map key yields the zero value,
so raising FeatureCompatibleVersion to 13 or beyond would print "please
upgrade MongoShake to version >= " with no version at all.
CurrentVersion now matches the shipped template at 14 rather than bumping the
template to 15. v2.8.9 already released with conf.version=14 and no new keys
have landed since, so moving the template would only diverge develop from the
released artifact. Key 13 is recorded as never-shipped because 0fbb387 stepped
straight over it.
Three guards, none needing MongoDB so they run in the minimal CI from #1026:
the counters must agree and stay ordered; both Lowest*Version maps must be
total over 0..CurrentVersion with non-empty values; and every config tag above
the "inner variables, not open to user" marker must appear in the template.
That last check matches unanchored, because the template documents options
that already have a usable default as commented examples such as
"# incr_sync.lazy_oplog_parse = true". All 90 user-facing tags pass, and the
12 absent ones all sit below the marker.
Red/green verified in both directions: reverting CurrentVersion to 12 fails
TestFcvCountersAgree, and deleting map key 14 fails
TestLowestVersionMapsAreTotal.

client CA path. It was also unread -- grep finds only the declaration -- which
is the only reason nothing broke.
Fixing the tag would have been worse than deleting the field: it would leave an
unread option behind a plausible-looking key, so setting
mongo_ssl_client_ca_file in a conf would be silently ignored rather than
visibly absent from the template. Client-certificate support does not exist
anywhere in the connection path either. NewMongoCommunityConn takes a single
sslRootFile, and addCACertFromFile only ever populates tls.Config.RootCAs --
there is no ClientCAs and no Certificates, so a client CA had nothing to be
applied to.
The sibling fields tunnel.mongo_ssl_root_ca_file and
checkpoint.storage.url.mongo_ssl_root_ca_file have unique tags and are both
read, so they are untouched.
TestConfigTagsAreUnique reflects over Configuration and fails on any repeated
tag; red before this change, green after. Real mTLS needs
tls.Config.Certificates threaded through NewMongoCommunityConn and its roughly
20 call sites, which is a feature and belongs in its own issue.

* fix: pass the executor metric maps to calculateTop3 by pointer (#1023)
calculateTop3 took a sync.Map by value and all six call sites in the /executor
HTTP handler passed the struct field itself. Copying a sync.Map copies its
mutex along with its read/dirty internals, so the copy's read pointer is a
snapshot from the instant of the copy: a promotion or CAS on the original
afterwards is invisible to it, and the top-3 counts the handler reports can be
stale or miss entries. The copy is taken while the sync goroutines are
concurrently storing into those same maps.
go vet reported 11 copylocks findings from this one signature -- six at the
call sites in executor.go, the declaration itself, and four in
executor_test.go. All 11 are gone. The remaining shift finding in
collision_matrix.go is #1024, and the 946 unkeyed-fields findings on
bson/primitive.E literals are pre-existing.
No deterministic failing test is writable for the staleness itself, since
whether a copied sync.Map observes later writes depends on internal promotion
state, so the guard here is go vet rather than a unit test. The existing
calculateTop3 tests still cover the selection logic and pass unchanged apart
from taking the address of their local map.

* fix: widen before shifting when signing a BSON Timestamp (#1024)
The Timestamp branch of calculateSignature read int64(o.T<<32). T is a uint32,
and Go defines a shift count at or above the operand width as zero rather than
leaving it undefined, so the seconds component never reached the signature --
only I did. Two timestamps a whole second apart but sharing an increment hashed
identically, and the collision matrix reads an identical signature as "same
unique index value" and serialises the two writes.
The direction is safe: signatures only ever become less distinct, never more,
so a genuine conflict cannot be missed and the cost is unnecessary
serialisation. Reachability is narrow as well. sanitize.go:594 derives
IncrSyncCollisionEnable from IncrSyncExecutor != 1, sanitize.go:321 normalises
an unset incr_sync.executor to 1, and that key is an inner option absent from
conf/collector.conf, so collision detection is off unless explicitly enabled --
and it then also needs a unique index whose column value is a BSON Timestamp.
Present since 169ffa2 (2022-05-10).
Widening first makes T dominate. It is not exact for realistic values: float64
represents integers only below 2^53, and a wall-clock T of ~1.7e9 shifted left
by 32 is ~7.5e18, so the increment rounds away. Preserving both components
would mean moving the signature off float64, which is more change than this
warrants -- newUniqueIdentifier already formats each signature with %f, six
decimals, so the scheme is approximate by construction. The test asserts
exactness only for small T and records why.
Changing the computation is safe at all because signatures never leave the
process: OplogUniqueIdentifier carries no serialisation tags, is never
marshalled, and its signatureTable only keys an in-memory map inside
BarrierMatrix.split. Nothing persisted and no routing decision depends on the
old values.
go vet's shift finding is gone, joining the copylocks findings cleared by
#1023; what remains is the 946 pre-existing unkeyed-fields findings on
bson/primitive.E literals.

* ci: add a minimal build/format/DB-free-test workflow (#1026)
The repository has had no CI at all, and .gitignore's blanket *.yml meant a
workflow file added today would be silently untracked. The negation for
.github/workflows/*.yml is part of this change for that reason.
The cost of having no gate is concrete: v2.8.7 and v2.8.8 both shipped a
collector.conf that made collector exit 254 at startup (#998), three merged
pull requests landed files that were not gofmt-clean (#1025), and go vet found
a sync.Map copied by value (#1023) and a shift by the operand width (#1024)
that both reached develop.
Scope is deliberately the part that needs no database: go build, a gofmt check
over tracked files only, and the four packages verified to pass with every
MONGOSHAKE_TEST_URL* unset -- collector/configure, which carries
TestShippedTemplateParses from #998 plus the fcv and config-tag guards from
#1021 and #1022, then collector/filter, collector/transform and
collector/spool. ./common is excluded because it dials a real server.
setup-go reads go.work rather than go.mod. go.work is tracked and declares
go 1.24.5 while go.mod says 1.21, so installing 1.21 would make the toolchain
reject the workspace file before it built anything.
go vet is not in the gate, and the workflow records why: it exits 1 with 946
unkeyed-fields findings on bson/primitive.E positional literals, which are
idiomatic in MongoDB code. A permanently red gate gets ignored. The
MongoDB-backed suite is out of scope too -- one service container cannot
provide a replica set, a config server and a sharded cluster, so the release
gate stays a local run.
Verified locally by running each step verbatim: build OK, gofmt clean across
all 170 tracked .go files, and the four packages ok in about 1.4s with the
environment variables unset.

evidence.text: - name: Test SQLite storage maintenance
perf(storage): replace clear-time VACUUM with batched purge and incremental reclaim (#494)
* perf(rusqlite): read last_insert_rowid lazily on the owning handle
Transaction::execute no longer issues an extra SELECT last_insert_rowid()
after every statement. Connection and Transaction now query the rowid on
demand from the exact physical handle that ran the INSERT (the held
transaction handle, or the single pooled handle), falling back to the last
rowid observed from statement results if the lookup fails.
Add shim tests for rowid semantics and run them in CI.
* fix(rusqlite): pin each connection to one physical SQLite handle
SQLx pools default to a 30 min max lifetime and 10 min idle timeout, which
silently replaced the single pooled handle. That lost connection-scoped
state (last_insert_rowid, busy_timeout, temp_store, journal_size_limit)
and wiped in-memory databases. Disable both so a Connection keeps one
handle for its whole life, like a real sqlite3 handle.
* perf(storage): replace clear-time VACUUM with batched purge and incremental reclaim
Clearing request logs ran `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE); VACUUM` after deleting
every payload row inside one transaction. With full payload storage that
rewrote a multi-GB file, needed as much free disk, held the write lock long
enough for gateway writes to hit the 3 s busy timeout, and with
temp_store=MEMORY could hold the transient copy in RAM.
- clear/prune now only make old data unreachable in a short transaction
(generation bump or retention watermark plus per-table rowid bounds in the
new request_log_payload_purges table, migration 142) and delete payload
rows in adaptive batches with secure_delete enabled; blobs are swept with a
reference check inside each delete transaction
- rows waiting for the purge are invisible to every reader and are never
chosen as parents of new manifests; work left over after the 10 s budget
(or after a restart) is continued by a background maintenance thread, and
errors after the first commit no longer fail the clear
- the maintenance thread also runs retention pruning off the request path,
retries busy WAL checkpoints and returns free pages with small
incremental_vacuum steps; new databases use auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL
- every connection sets journal_size_limit; space accounting uses live pages
(page_count - freelist_count), never the file size
- admin-only storage/spaceUsage and storage/reclaim RPCs and a settings card
show used/reclaimable space and offer an explicit, disk-checked one-time
rebuild for databases created by older versions
* fix(storage): keep missing path components when matching a disk mount
When a path did not exist, normalized_components canonicalized its parent
and dropped the last component, so a missing mount point such as
/definitely-not-a-mount compared equal to / and could win the
longest-prefix match. Resolve the deepest existing ancestor instead and
re-append the components below it.

### Overriding message serializer

Roarr is opinionated about how it serializes (converts objects to JSON string) log messages, e.g. in Node.js it uses a schema based serializer, which is very fast, but does not allow custom top-level properties.

Replace grep based e2e test selectors w/ file based (#4003)
This changes the way we select e2e tests in CI. Previously we would grep
for the string in the describe which is quite brittle. This method uses
a file based approach which should help us scale better as we add more
tests.
<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes CI orchestration and how E2E tests are selected/executed;
failures are most likely to surface as missing coverage or mis-bucketed
tests rather than product runtime issues.
> **Overview**
> Framework CLI CI now runs E2E test “buckets” via explicit test file
entrypoints (`test:ts-default`, `test:ts-tests:*`, `test:py-*`) instead
of `mocha --grep`, making test selection less brittle and easier to
scale.
> This refactors `framework-cli-e2e` tests to support targeted execution
via `E2E_TEMPLATE_TARGET`/`E2E_TEMPLATE_LANGUAGE`, adds small per-bucket
wrapper test files, and introduces a `validate-ci-bucket.js` guard to
fail fast when a referenced test file is missing.
> CI log inspection is hardened by replacing inline `cat
~/.moose/*-cli.log` with a reusable composite action (`dump-cli-logs`)
that succeeds when no logs are present.

evidence.text: feat(bundler): add Vite and Rsbuild integrations (#300)
* feat(bundler): add Vite and Rsbuild integrations
Add six additive packages giving Esmx first-class support for Vite and
Rsbuild alongside the existing Rspack integration, without touching any
existing package code:
Base packages (App contract: build / start / dev):
- @esmx/vite: Vite/Rollup integration with native ESM module-federation
output, esmx-format manifest, and real module-level HMR in dev (Vite
dev server in middleware mode, base-aligned, ssrLoadModule rendering).
- @esmx/rsbuild: Rsbuild integration over the rspack kernel, reusing the
proven webpack-hot-middleware HMR mechanism.
Framework presets (thin adapters injecting the framework plugin):
- @esmx/vite-react, @esmx/vite-vue (@vitejs/plugin-react / -vue)
- @esmx/rsbuild-react, @esmx/rsbuild-vue (@rsbuild/plugin-react / -vue)
Each package emits native ESM federation chunks (shared deps externalized
as bare specifiers, resolved by the import map) consumed unchanged by
@esmx/core. Verified end-to-end with six example apps
(ssr-{vite,rsbuild}-{html,react,vue}) via esmx build + esmx start,
covering plain HTML, React and Vue plus pkg:react/react-dom/vue
real-package federation.
* docs(core): document Esmx.write() and command getter
Add the missing async write() method (counterpart of writeSync, already used
in the postBuild example) and the command getter (current command, distinct
from the COMMAND enum) to the @esmx/core API reference, in both en and zh.
Verified all other documented core APIs against packages/core/src.
* docs(vite): add @esmx/vite API reference (en + zh)
Document the @esmx/vite package API (BuildTarget, ViteAppConfigContext,
ViteAppOptions, ViteHtmlAppOptions, createViteApp, createViteHtmlApp, vite
re-export) generated from packages/vite/src, and register it in the App
section nav. Verified with a full docs build.
* docs(rsbuild): add @esmx/rsbuild API reference (en + zh)
Document the @esmx/rsbuild package API (BuildTarget, RsbuildAppConfigContext,
RsbuildAppOptions, RsbuildHtmlAppOptions, createRsbuildApp,
createRsbuildHtmlApp, rspack re-export) generated from packages/rsbuild/src,
and register it in the App section nav. Verified with a full docs build.
* docs(vite): add @esmx/vite-react and @esmx/vite-vue API references (en + zh)
Document the React and Vue 3 presets (createViteReactApp/createViteVueApp,
ViteReactAppOptions/ViteVueAppOptions, @esmx/vite re-exports) from their
src/index.ts, and register them in the App section nav after vite. Verified
with a full docs build.
* docs(rsbuild): add @esmx/rsbuild-react and @esmx/rsbuild-vue API references (en + zh)
Document the React and Vue 3 presets (createRsbuildReactApp/createRsbuildVueApp,
RsbuildReactAppOptions/RsbuildVueAppOptions, @esmx/rsbuild re-exports) from
their src/index.ts, and register them in the App nav after rsbuild. All six new
bundler packages are now documented. Verified with a full docs build.
* docs(router): document Route.confirm and Route.layer
Add the two public readonly Route properties (confirm: RouteConfirmHook|null,
layer: RouteLayerOptions|null) that were missing from the Route reference, in
both en and zh. Audited the rest of the @esmx/router docs (Router/Route members,
RouterMode/RouteType enums, error classes, option types) against
packages/router/src — all accurate (deprecated href/pathname correctly omitted).
* docs(router-react): document the useLink hook
Add the useLink(props: RouterLinkProps): RouterLinkResolved headless hook to
the router-react hooks reference (en + zh); it powers RouterLink and mirrors
@esmx/router-vue's useLink, which was already documented. Audited router-react
and router-vue exports against src — all other public symbols are covered.
* docs(guide): reference official Vite and Rsbuild integrations in build-tools section
Update the 'Decoupling of Build Tools' essentials guide (en + zh) to point at
the shipped @esmx/vite and @esmx/rsbuild integrations and their framework
presets, with a switch-to-Vite example. Audited the rest of the build/router
guides — builder names and the chain hook match the real exports.
* docs: add bilingual README for the six new bundler packages
Add README.md + README.zh-CN.md for @esmx/vite, @esmx/rsbuild,
@esmx/{vite,rsbuild}-{react,vue}, modeled on the existing package READMEs
(badges, features, install, quick start, docs link). Usage examples use the
real createViteApp/createRsbuildReactApp/... APIs from each package.
* docs: list Vite and Rsbuild packages in the root README
Add @esmx/{vite,rsbuild} and their React/Vue presets to the Core Packages
table, and broaden the high-performance-build feature to mention Rspack,
Rsbuild and Vite (en + zh).
* docs(examples): fix README for the new Vite/Rsbuild example apps
The React/Vue example READMEs were copied verbatim from the csr templates
(wrong title, build tool and port). Rewrite all six (ssr-{vite,rsbuild}-{html,
react,vue}) with the correct project name, build tool, framework and dev port;
add READMEs for the two HTML examples that had none.
* docs: fix fabricated Quick Start APIs in existing package READMEs
The core/rspack/rspack-react/rspack-vue READMEs used non-existent APIs
(createEsmx, createRspack, createRspackReact, createRspackVue). Replace with
the real entry.node.ts devApp pattern using createRspackHtmlApp /
createRspackReactApp / createRspackVue3App, driven by the esmx CLI; also fix a
stray Chinese link in the English core README (en + zh).
* example(micro-app): add ssr-micro-vite-html remote (Vite + HTML)
A Vite-built HTML micro-app remote that shares ssr-micro-shared's router via
the import map, to be composed by the hub alongside the Rspack remotes.
Mirrors ssr-micro-html; only the bundler (@esmx/vite, createViteHtmlApp) and
route path (/vite-html/) differ.
* example(micro-app): add ssr-micro-vite-react remote (Vite + React)
Vite-built React micro-app remote (federates react/react-dom, shares the
router via the import map). Mirrors ssr-micro-react; only the bundler
(@esmx/vite-react, createViteReactApp) and route path (/vite-react/) differ.
* example(micro-app): add ssr-micro-vite-vue remote (Vite + Vue3)
Vite-built Vue 3 micro-app remote (federates vue, server-only
@vue/server-renderer, SFC compilation, shares the router via the import map).
Mirrors ssr-micro-vue3; only the bundler (@esmx/vite-vue, createViteVueApp)
and route path (/vite-vue/) differ.
* example(micro-app): add ssr-micro-rsbuild-html remote (Rsbuild + HTML)
Rsbuild-built HTML micro-app remote that shares ssr-micro-shared's router via
the import map. Mirrors ssr-micro-html; only the bundler (@esmx/rsbuild,
createRsbuildHtmlApp) and route path (/rsbuild-html/) differ.
* example(micro-app): add ssr-micro-rsbuild-react remote (Rsbuild + React)
Rsbuild-built React micro-app remote (federates react/react-dom, shares the
router via the import map). Mirrors ssr-micro-react; only the bundler
(@esmx/rsbuild-react, createRsbuildReactApp) and route path (/rsbuild-react/)
differ.
* example(micro-app): add ssr-micro-rsbuild-vue remote (Rsbuild + Vue3)
Rsbuild-built Vue 3 micro-app remote (federates vue, server-only
@vue/server-renderer, shares the router via the import map). Mirrors
ssr-micro-vue3; only the bundler (@esmx/rsbuild-vue, createRsbuildVueApp) and
route path (/rsbuild-vue/) differ. Completes the six new bundler remotes.
* fix(bundler): correct CJS/SSR federation for Vite and Rsbuild; wire 5 micro-app remotes into hub
@esmx/vite:
- Federate pkg exports via a virtual module with explicit static named exports
(discovered by loading the package in Node), so a CommonJS package like react
exposes `useState` etc. — fixes `import { useState } from 'react'` in SSR.
- Disable Vite SSR auto-externalization (ssr.noExternal) so subpaths such as
react-dom/server / react/jsx-runtime are inlined and import the single
federated react/react-dom instead of a second node_modules copy (which broke
React's hooks dispatcher).
@esmx/rsbuild:
- optimization.usedExports=false so federation chunks keep exports consumed
only by other bundles (e.g. vue's ssrUtils), and cache=!isProd for
deterministic production output.
Wire vite-html/react/vue and rsbuild-html/react into ssr-micro-hub: one host
composing remotes built by Rspack + Vite + Rsbuild, sharing one router via the
import map. ssr-micro-rsbuild-vue is linked but not yet routed (its Vue SSR
needs a dedicated fix tracked separately).
* fix(rsbuild): make Vue SSR federation work; wire rsbuild-vue into hub
Root-cause fixes so an Rsbuild-built Vue 3 remote SSR-renders when federated:
- @esmx/rsbuild: the externals function now only externalizes a federation
specifier when it has an issuer (imported by another module). A pkg export's
own entry module has no issuer and must be built, not externalized into an
empty re-export — mirrors @esmx/rspack's module-link. This lets pkg entries
stay BARE specifiers so resolve.alias applies to them.
- @esmx/rsbuild-vue: alias `vue$` to the runtime-only build and compile SFCs
with isServerBuild on server/node targets. @rsbuild/plugin-vue otherwise
resolves vue to the full build (dragging the template compiler into the
federated chunk) and never sets isServerBuild, which broke the
@vue/server-renderer ↔ vue `ssrUtils` linkage.
- Fix a missing `...rsbuildVueRoutes` spread in the hub so the route is
actually registered (the import alone was tree-shaken).
All six new remotes (vite/rsbuild × html/react/vue) now SSR-render real
framework content in ssr-micro-hub, composed alongside the Rspack remotes and
sharing one router via the import map.
* chore: remove loop scaffolding handoff docs
These were internal task-orchestration notes accidentally committed via the
lint-staged 'git add .' step; they are not part of the deliverable.
* fix(vite,rsbuild): align manifest chunk keys with core SSR chunkName
The manifest plugins keyed chunks by output name and never injected
import.meta.chunkName, so RenderContext.commit() could not match the
client manifest's chunk keys against the SSR-executed chunk set —
federated code-split chunk CSS/resources were silently dropped.
- key chunks by their source path relative to root (mirrors
@esmx/rspack generateIdentifier, matching core's hardcoded
`name@src/entry.client.ts` seed)
- inject import.meta.chunkName into the server build so commit()
collects the matching client chunk CSS/resources
- resolvePkgNames: warn instead of silently returning [] on require
failure (no silent failure)
- rsbuild dev: log watch errors instead of swallowing them
- ssr-rsbuild-html: fix copied-over title 'Vite' -> 'Rsbuild'
- add unit tests for externals predicate + chunkSourceKey (regression
guard for the chunk-key fix)
* refactor(examples): make standalone vite/rsbuild react & vue demos true SSR
The standalone ssr-vite-* / ssr-rsbuild-* react & vue examples were
client-side rendered (createRoot / createApp + empty #app) despite the
ssr- prefix. Make their behavior match their name:
- react: renderToString(<App/>) on the server into #app, hydrateRoot on
the client (was createRoot)
- vue: createSSRApp + @vue/server-renderer renderToString on the server,
createSSRApp mount hydration on the client (was createApp)
- update titles/meta/copy from 'CSR / client-side' to 'SSR / server-side'
Verified: all 4 emit server-rendered markup in #app (curl), hydrate in a
real browser with no console warnings/hydration mismatch, and the counter
increments after hydration (single framework instance via the import map).
* chore(examples): drop stale csr naming from standalone ssr demos
- fix one missed 'client-side rendering' string in ssr-vite-vue
- rename tsconfig self-reference path aliases from *-csr-demo to the
actual package name (ssr-vite-react/ssr-rsbuild-react/ssr-vite-vue/
ssr-rsbuild-vue) so they match package.json and the esmx module name
* fix(examples): resolve unhead UseHeadInput type mismatch in vue micro-apps
buildSeoHead returned unhead core's UseHeadInput (= ResolvableHead, which
permits getter/function values). @unhead/vue's useHead expects its own
Vue-reactive UseHeadInput, and core ResolvableHead is not assignable to it
(@unhead/react's useHead uses the core type, so react was unaffected) —
breaking `pnpm lint:type` on all three vue micro examples.
- type buildSeoHead's return as unhead's SerializableHead (the plain,
static head it actually produces), which IS assignable to both
@unhead/react and @unhead/vue useHead inputs
- align the unhead core dep to ^3.1.3 across the micro examples so it
matches the @unhead/vue / @unhead/react 3.1.3 adapters (was ^3.1.0,
resolving to a stale 3.1.0)
Full `pnpm lint:type` now passes repo-wide; hub still SSRs every route
with SEO meta intact.
* fix(vite): compute SRI integrity after Vite finalizes chunk code
The manifest plugin hashed chunk.code in a default-order generateBundle,
but Vite's build-import-analysis rewrites dynamic-import preload markers
(__VITE_PRELOAD__) into the final dependency array in its own
generateBundle. When ours ran first, the SRI hash was computed over the
pre-rewrite code, so code-split chunks (which carry the preload array)
failed the browser's integrity check and were blocked — e.g.
ssr-micro-vite-vue's chunks/routes.*.mjs on the deployed preview. Entry
chunks were unaffected (no preload-marker rewrite).
Run generateBundle with order:'post' so integrity is computed over the
finalized code that is actually written and served.
Verified: all .mjs/.css across all 6 vite-based examples now have
matching SRI (was mismatching on code-split chunks). Added a regression
test asserting the hook stays order:'post'.
* fix(core): scope code-split chunk files in the client import map
A module-level scope was only expanded onto the module's export files, so
code-split chunk files (Vite/Rollup facade+impl splits, e.g.
chunks/routes.*.mjs) — which still 'import "vue"' — had no import-map
scope. The browser then failed with 'Failed to resolve module specifier
"vue"' when such a chunk loaded. rspack's all-in-one output emits no
extra chunks, so only Vite remotes were affected.
createClientImportMap now adds, per manifest, the module's bare-specifier
scope to each of its code-split chunk files — done AFTER compression so it
never skews the global-promotion heuristic (which must keep a multi-version
dep like 'vue' scoped, not hoisted). Adds ImportMapManifest.chunks and a
regression test.
Verified in a real browser: /vite-vue/, /rsbuild-vue/ and the pre-existing
/vue3/ hub routes load with no console errors and hydrate (counter works).
* test(core): expand code-split chunk scope coverage
Add cases for addCodeSplitChunkScopes: skip when a global import already
resolves the specifier (single-module promotion), no-op for all-in-one
manifests without chunks (rspack), and applying every module external to
its chunk. Purely additive — existing import-map cases unchanged (176 pass).
* feat(micro-app): add vite/rsbuild remotes to hub navigation
The 6 new vite/rsbuild remotes had routes but were missing from the hub
sidebar nav, so they were only reachable by direct URL. Add them with a
bundler-prefixed label (Vite/Rsbuild) so the heterogeneous federation —
one host composing 3 bundlers x html/react/vue — is discoverable and
SPA-navigable from the UI.
Verified in a real browser: all 15 nav links present; clicking 'Vite Vue'
client-side navigates to /vite-vue/ and renders with no console errors.
* refactor(micro-app): extract shared host (render/hydrate) used by hub
Add ssr-micro-shared/src/host.ts with renderHost(rc, routes, {standalone})
and hydrateHost(routes, {standalone}), extracted verbatim from the hub's
entry.server/entry.client so the hub and (next) each standalone remote
share one framework-agnostic host implementation — single source of truth.
- standalone mode prepends a '/' -> primary-route redirect and sets a
router-context flag; the shared Layout hides cross-remote nav in that
mode (those remotes aren't mounted, their links would 404)
- hub now delegates to renderHost/hydrateHost (full nav, standalone:false)
Verified in a real browser: hub /vue3/ + SPA nav to /vite-vue/ render with
15 nav links, counter hydrates, console clean — behavior unchanged.
* feat(micro-app): ssr-micro-vite-vue runs standalone + fix dev SSR bugs
Wire the reference remote (vite-vue) to run on its own via the shared host
(entry.server -> renderHost, entry.client -> hydrateHost, both standalone;
server() reads PORT, default 3012). Two real bugs surfaced once a micro
remote actually SSR-renders in dev (previously their entries were no-op
stubs), both fixed:
- @esmx/router validateSsrRootElement: found the root's closing tag via
indexOf('</tag>'), matching the FIRST (inner) same-tag close and wrongly
reporting trailing content — so any single root nesting same-tag children
(a <div> wrapping <div>s, very common) was rejected in dev, blanking the
SSR output and forcing a client full-mount. Now matches the root close by
depth. Dev-only validator; prod unaffected. +2 regression tests (978 pass).
- @esmx/vite dev: the browser HMR client (@vite/client) was injected into
modules even during SSR (ssrLoadModule), crashing the SSR module runner
('Failed to resolve /<name>/@vite/client'). Skip injection when ssr.
- shared host: standalone '/' renders the remote's primary route (URL
rewrite, not a redirect route, so SSR stays a 200 render).
Verified in a real browser: vite-vue standalone, prod AND dev, renders SSR
+ hydrates (counter), nav shows only itself with a Standalone badge, console
clean.
* feat(micro-app): all 14 remaining remotes run standalone
Wire every micro remote (html/lit/vue2/vue3/react/preact/preact-htm/solid/
svelte + vite-html/react + rsbuild-html/react/vue) to run on its own via the
shared host: entry.server -> renderHost(standalone), entry.client ->
hydrateHost(standalone). server() reads PORT (defaults 3001-3015 so all can
run at once). The 3 html remotes previously had no server() at all (pure
federation libs) — added one.
Each remote now: composes in the hub (full nav) AND runs standalone (own
page, sidebar shows only itself + a Standalone badge, '/' -> its route).
Verified in a real browser — all 15 standalone (3 bundlers x 9 frameworks):
SSR renders, hydrates (counter 0->1 where interactive), console clean; and
hub regression: 15-link nav, composition + hydration intact.
* fix(micro-app): align host.ts Window global type with hub global.d.ts
renderHost/hydrateHost declared window.__ESMX_CONTEXT__ as `any`, conflicting
with the hub's existing `Record<string, unknown>` global (TS2717). Match it.
Full pnpm lint:type now passes.
* fix(router-react): align react devDep to ^19.2.6 (dedupe for dev SSR)
@esmx/router-react's react/react-dom devDep (^19.1.0) resolved to react
19.2.4 while the micro examples use 19.2.6. In dev SSR (no federation import
map for react), node loaded router-react/dist's react (19.2.4) and the
component's react (19.2.6) as TWO instances → null hooks dispatcher
('Cannot read properties of null (reading useCallback)'). Bumping the devDep
to ^19.2.6 dedupes them to one instance.
Fixes vite-react standalone dev SSR (verified: renders + no dispatcher
error). rspack/rsbuild react dev still hit a separate vm-import CJS issue
(next).
* feat: vite/rsbuild bundler support + @esmx/pkg-wrapper for federation pkg exports
New package
- @esmx/pkg-wrapper: generates static ESM re-export wrappers for
federation `pkg:*` exports so vite/rspack/rsbuild can statically
enumerate names (CJS conditional NODE_ENV branches intersected, ESM
`export *` chains followed, Node 24 condition-map walk for ESM-only
exports).
Adapters
- @esmx/vite: register each `pkg:*` export as a virtual module
(`\0esmx-pkg-reexport:<spec>`) backed by the generated wrapper;
external-require plugin patches rolldown's `__toESM` ternary and
rewrites the minified `<alias>("<external>")` call sites that bypass
`module.register`.
- @esmx/rspack, @esmx/rsbuild: install wrappers via
`rspack-plugin-virtual-module` under
`<root>/node_modules/.esmx-virtual-<name>/`; externals skip
wrapper-issued requests to avoid cycles. `createChainConfig` /
`createRsbuildConfig` made async.
- @esmx/vite ^8 + @vitejs/plugin-react ^6, tsconfig moduleResolution
bundler.
Examples
- ssr-vite-react, ssr-rsbuild-react, ssr-vite-html bumped to vite ^8 /
react ^19 for dedup with dev SSR.
Validation
- 21/21 prod builds, 20/20 standalone runtime, 20/20 hub-composed
cross-remote, 12/12 dev-SSR matrix (vite/rspack/rsbuild/lit), 4/4
browser hydration combos, lint:type clean, 1438 unit tests passing.
Closes #40 (rspack/rsbuild dev SSR CJS named-export resolution).
* fix(create-esmx): bump react-csr template to react ^19.2.6
Aligns the source template with the materialized examples/templates/
react-csr/package.json (lockfile already pins ^19.2.6 after the dev SSR
dedupe work). CI's frozen-lockfile install otherwise rehydrates the
template at ^18 and fails the lockfile-consistency check.
* fix(svelte-example): restore `let` for $state rune binding
Biome lint-staged auto-converted `let count = $state(0)` to
`const` because it can't see the rune-side reassignment, breaking
the svelte 5 compile (`constant_assignment: Cannot assign to constant`)
when the +/- buttons mutate `count` at line 48/49. Restore `let`
with a biome-ignore comment so future lint-staged runs leave it alone.
* feat: agent-era redesign — UX/docs/CI overhaul
Redesigns demo UX + landing + design system to make Esmx's "zero proprietary
API surface" thesis legible at a glance. Lands the full CI regression matrix
(build + curl smoke + hydration markers + Lighthouse + visual baselines) and
the public llms.md guide with code-block auto-validation.
Highlights:
- A: design system in ssr-micro-shared (74 tokens, 42 classes, internal docs at docs/design/)
- B/C: 15 micros + 6 standalone demos redesigned around the same shared classes
- D: hub landing + demo index + matrix section rewritten with agent-era narrative
- E1: examples/docs/src/{en,zh}/llms.md — ~280-line per-language guide for user agents
- E2-E3: api/ + guide/ doc audits with high-priority fixes
- E4: create-esmx templates aligned to the new design
- E5: error-message rewrite across 10 worst offenders
- F1: regression.yml — types/units + build + smoke (22 server matrix via scripts/smoke.mjs)
- F2: playwright visual regression infra (config + spec + scripts/start-all.mjs + visual-bootstrap.yml)
- F3: .lighthouserc.json — a11y/SEO >= 95, LCP <= 2500ms, CLS <= 0.1
- F4: scripts/validate-llms.mjs — esbuild parse + JSON.parse over every fenced code block
- G1-G7: federation-native CSS contract — each remote owns its CSS via manifest chunks[].css[]

The Svelte 5 compiler closes the outer <script> block at the first

* fix(ci): upload baselines from playwright's spec-relative snapshots dir
* feat(visual): commit 23 Linux/Chromium baselines + remove one-shot bootstrap trigger

2. **Manifest** as the deployment contract — adds `protocol`, `version`, and

3. **Deterministic link-time resolution** — auto-wiring from declarations,
hard build-time errors with fixes that always live in existing declarations,

* fix(pkg-wrapper): fall back to package root entry when subpath resolves to an unlexable bundle
After 60d02d4ba taught pickEntry() to follow subpath specifiers into the
exports map, packages like vue map 'vue/dist/vue.runtime.esm-browser.prod.js'
to a single-line minified file that es-module-lexer rejects with a parse
error. inspectPkg then degraded to default-only re-export and downstream
'import { version } from vue' crashed shared-modules's postBuild.
The fix retries with the package's bare specifier (root entry) when the
first lex attempt throws. The root entry is the lean ESM build whose
named-export surface is a superset of (or identical to) the deep subpath's,
so the federation wrapper still emits a complete static names list. The
bundler ultimately resolves to the deep subpath via the host's import map,
so the wrapper only needs to satisfy the lexer.
Adds a synthetic 'minified-subpath-pkg' fixture with an intentionally
unterminated-template dist/* target that exercises the fallback path; the
test asserts no warning is logged when the retry succeeds.

The single-owner shared packages over-shared the thin per-framework
provide/inject binding adapters (@unhead/vue, @esmx/router-vue;

provide/inject Symbols stay self-consistent. The shared STATE (the

evidence.text: //   serial    5 of 5 green
//   parallel  2 of 4 red - content-lifecycle could not read back the value it had
//             just written to its own data record (twice), and the csrf quote form
//             did not save (once)
// Both failures are the shared fixtures being used from two places at once, and
// neither has ever happened serially. Parallel finishes in about a third of the
// time, which is not worth a suite that is wrong half the time it runs.
// Making it genuinely parallel-safe means giving each worker its own fixtures, which
// undoes the sharing that keeps the tables flat; it is a bigger change than this one
// and wants doing deliberately, not as a side effect.
Stop the browser suites leaving their fixtures in the database
Running the suite twice in a row did not leave the database where it found
it. Every run added a few hundred rows, and once enough had built up the
suite started failing in ways that said nothing about the software: the
subscription table reached 208 rows named 'CSRF Test Subscription', every
customer and invoice screen renders a checkbox per subscription, and
quote-to-invoice.spec.ts timed out at 180 seconds. Deleting the leftovers
took that test to 11 seconds.
Twenty-one of the thirty-nine specs grew a table on every run. Each one now
either reuses a named fixture or deletes what it made, checked by running
each spec twice and asserting the row counts do not move. leftovers.spec.ts
is the guard: it counts the rows carrying the suites' own fixture names and
fails while there are too many, so the next spec that stops cleaning up says
so instead of making some unrelated test slow.
Reuse is asserted, not assumed. Three helpers claimed to reuse a record and
quietly made a new one every run - the company lookup ran a regex over a
screen that renders no company_id at all, a data field helper documented
itself as "reused across runs" while posting the field again each time, and
a fieldset was created with a `name` the handler drops instead of `title`,
so none of them could ever be found again. Two cleanups deleted nothing and
said they had.
Nine application bugs turned up behind the cleanups, each one a delete that
did not take its dependants:
- deleting a website raised an ArgumentCountError before the DELETE, so it
never worked at all - records-lifecycle.spec.ts had left that assertion
out with a note saying the cause was unclear
- delete_customer() left the whole customer_config block behind
- delete_invoice() left invoice_payment_method
- delete_job() left job_tax
- delete_data_type() left its permission, its menu config and data_access
- delete_user() left _dashboard_item_hide and user_perm
- delete_newsletter() left newsletter_send_member - a standing todo - and
removed only the first send of several
- opening the encrypt popup inserted a row on every GET, where
save_encrypt_value() beside it has always found the field first
contract.spec.ts was failing on a 37-character assertion against a list that
trims notes to 35; the first test in the file passes only because its string
is exactly 35. Fixed in the test - the record was always correct.
Workers are pinned to 1 everywhere rather than only in CI. The suites share
named fixtures, which is what keeps the counts flat and what makes them
unsafe side by side: four parallel runs went 2 red, five serial runs went 5
green. The reasoning is in the config.
Verified: five serial runs of the whole suite, 209 passed and 2 skipped each
time, with no row left behind in any table.

evidence.text: // The suite shares one app + one database; parallel workers would race on the
// fixtures they seed.
Add test suites for the collaborative editor + CI
The collaborative editor is the part of the app most likely to break
silently: it only misbehaves with several clients, often only under a
specific join order or timing. This adds two runners covering it, and a
CI workflow that runs them on every pull request.
Vitest (`npm test`, ~15s, no external service):
- tests/unit — the segment projection (`docToSegments`) whose purity and
determinism is what makes clients converge on per-word timestamps, the
transport codecs including the AES-GCM one used for E2E transcripts,
and the full sharing permission matrix.
- tests/integration — the real protocol: the app's own Socket.io server
on an ephemeral port, real socket.io clients with real JWT tokens, and
real Y.Docs driven by the app's provider. Covers seeding authority,
late joiners, convergence under concurrent edits, authority hand-off,
single-save-leader invariant, room isolation, remote carets, and that
an encrypted transcript only ever crosses the relay as ciphertext.
Playwright (`npm run test:e2e`, ~1.5min): two browser contexts editing
one shared transcript through the whole app, asserting propagation both
ways, character-for-character convergence, late-join, remote carets,
persistence via the save leader, and the read-only guard.
Test database: PGlite (real PostgreSQL compiled to WASM, in-process)
exposed on a TCP socket, so `@prisma/adapter-pg` connects unchanged and
the schema is applied with `prisma db push`. SQLite would have required
changing the schema itself — Prisma supports neither enums nor scalar
lists there, and sharing is queried with JSONB containment — so the
suite would have tested a different schema than production runs.
Three bugs the tests surfaced, fixed here:
- Socket auth ran inside an async `connection` handler, so the
`yjs:join` a client emits on connect could arrive before the handlers
were registered and be dropped — the editor then never seeded nor
synced. Authentication now runs in a Socket.io middleware, which
buffers packets until it resolves.
- The provider's teardown encoded its awareness state *before* removing
it, so the "drop my cursor" message re-announced the caret instead;
peers kept a ghost cursor until y-protocols' 30s timeout.
- `EditorAPI.execCommand` mutated the document without checking
editability. Document-level shortcuts bypass ProseMirror's own guard,
so a participant shared with a read-only role could type and delete —
and the change synced to everyone else and was persisted.
Also extracts the sharing access rules into lib/transcriptions/access.ts
(deduplicating the raw containment query) so they are testable, and
replaces the two `*.proto.ts` verification scripts, now superseded by
the Vitest suites.
